summary: Adds release-aware placement v3, tenant-scoped mixed-release SSO callbacks, short-lived tenant Cloud identity, plugin work handoff, plugin release-affinity declarations, and a trusted system frontend boundary for managed SaaS.
userImpact: Managed deployments can expose tenant administration pages from a release-neutral control plane without packaging those pages as an optional tenant marketplace plugin.
Existing OSS, EE, and native marketplace plugin behavior remains unchanged when no system frontend modules are configured.
Managed pooled deployments can bind each request to the exact tenant, shard, release, placement epoch, and release-assignment epoch without changing tenant SSO ownership.
Managed mixed-release deployments can keep each tenant's OIDC or SAML callback and asynchronous plugin work on that tenant's assigned release.

instructions: Managed operators may add same-origin trusted system module descriptors to the existing frontend runtime configuration document.
Managed mixed-release shards set EG_TENANT_PLACEMENT_RELEASE_ID, EG_TENANT_CLOUD_IDENTITY_AUDIENCE, and the secret EG_TENANT_RELEASE_CONTROLLER_TOKEN; self-hosted deployments leave them unset.
Register tenant-scoped OIDC and SAML callback URLs before opening Preview enrollment; the established global callbacks remain supported for existing deployments.

configuration: The optional systemFrontendModules runtime-config field declares reverse-DNS owner ids, same-origin JavaScript entry paths, and SHA-256 integrity values.
A configured module marked required fails application startup when its descriptor, integrity check, import, or activation fails; optional modules fail closed without affecting the OSS shell.
Managed release hosts require an exact release ID, Cloud identity audience, and dedicated private release-controller token.

changes: The enterprise frontend plugin API exports additive trusted system module descriptor and module contracts.
The frontend host can activate multiple owner-isolated system modules in addition to the existing singular EE compatibility bridge.
Placement assertion v3 and the tenant Cloud identity endpoint are additive; placement v1 and v2 remain supported.
Plugin manifest v1 accepts an optional releaseAffinity declaration for mixed-host, fallback, job, and event compatibility.
Tenant-scoped OIDC and SAML callback routes and the workload-only release-assignment route are additive; global callback routes remain available.

notes: The additive migration stores nullable release ID and assignment epoch on plugin event deliveries and scheduled jobs, and adds one tenant release-work assignment row per managed tenant.
Existing rows and unmanaged deployments remain valid because the new event/job columns are nullable and the assignment table is unused without a managed release ID.

security: System module entry URLs must resolve to the application origin and each downloaded module is verified against a configured SHA-256 digest before import.
Owner identifiers and extension keys are validated and cross-owner collisions fail atomically.
System modules receive the existing constrained host context and cannot register legacy feature or component replacements.
Tenant Cloud identity assertions are short lived and contain tenant, role, shard, release, and epoch claims but no SSO provider configuration, identity assertion, or secret.

The release-work handoff uses a dedicated constant-time bearer check, requires an exact configured host release, rejects stale epochs, and does not accept interactive or ordinary service-account tokens.
documentation: Frontend runtime configuration documents the optional trusted system module boundary, integrity requirements, failure behavior, and separation from tenant marketplace plugins.
Native SaaS tenancy, SSO, plugin authoring, configuration, and tenant workload lifecycle documentation cover release-aware routing, callbacks, and asynchronous work handoff.
knownLimitations: Content Security Policy must permit the host's integrity-verified module import mechanism when system modules are enabled.
The OSS repository provides the neutral extension mechanism; managed release policy, tenant lifecycle, and control-plane APIs remain deployment-owned concerns.
rollback: Remove systemFrontendModules from runtime configuration or roll back the frontend image; deployments without the field retain the previous startup path.
validation: Frontend-host unit coverage for descriptor validation, same-origin enforcement, SHA-256 verification, required and optional failure behavior, owner isolation, and coexistence with the EE bridge
Runtime-config unit coverage proving the new field is additive and omitted configurations retain prior behavior
Tenant-scoped OIDC and SAML callback, placement v3, Cloud identity, release-work handoff, plugin schedule/event affinity, and pooled tenancy coverage
Frontend host build, backend plugin runtime suite, migration portability checks, plugin SDK compatibility, and release-note contract validation
